name: ChromeForm
description: A turned metal form rotating in a studio built for it to reflect, with no image files to ship

notes: Most of this item is the room rather than the object. A mirror has no colour and no shading of its own, so chrome in an empty scene looks like grey plastic: there is nothing for it to be a reflection of

The environment is painted into a canvas at runtime and used as an equirectangular map, so nothing is shipped: no HDR, no cube faces, no image files at all. A dark surround, a brighter floor and a few soft strip lights, which is what a photographer would put round something shiny

The strips are what say metal. A gradient alone gives a smooth tonal wash that still reads as plastic; what reads as polished is a hard edge between light and dark sliding across a curve. The horizon step in the surround does the same job round the waist

Lamps are spaced on an irrational step. Evenly spaced lamps put evenly spaced highlights round the object, and evenly spaced highlights read as a pattern printed on it rather than as a room it is standing in

Prefiltered through PMREM rather than used raw, because otherwise roughness does nothing but darken: a raw map is sampled at one level however rough the surface claims to be, and the blurred levels are what a rough surface needs

A lathe, not a torus knot. A knot is what every WebGL demo reaches for and says nothing about anything; a revolved profile is how a metal object of this kind is actually made, it gives the long uninterrupted curves that show a reflection off best, and the profile is three numbers rather than a model file

ACES tone mapping, which is unusual here and is the one case that needs it. A mirror genuinely produces values above one, and clipping a strip light gives a flat white shape with a hard edge where the roll-off should be
Geometry and environment are rebuilt only when their inputs change, because update() can be called on every frame by a framework re-render and PMREM has no business running at 60Hz

Built for a dark ground and declared as one. The room is dark so that the strips read as light; on paper the background would have to be pale, and a pale fill behind a dark-roomed mirror looks like a hole cut in the page
One lathe mesh of 128 segments and one prefiltered environment, both rebuilt only when their inputs change. The per-frame work is a single draw of about twelve thousand triangles
Measured with `pnpm budget` at 1280 by 720: 1.2ms for a draw and a forced flush, against TerrainRelief at 1.80 on the same run

0.035 mean absolute change per frame on a 0 to 255 scale, worst 0.042, against TerrainRelief at 0.450 and DustMotes at 0.016. One of the quietest items here: a single object turning slowly against a flat fill changes very few pixels, which is what a backdrop wants
PMREM runs once per change of `studio` or `lamps`, not per frame. Animating either of those at 60Hz would be the one way to make this item expensive

background.description: The page behind the object. Nothing reflects it, so it is only a fill, but it wants to be close to the dark end of the room or the object reads as cut out and pasted on.

tint.description: The metal. Near white is chrome; warm it towards #e8c89a for brass and cool it for steel. On a fully metallic surface this multiplies the reflection rather than adding a colour of its own, which is why a saturated one looks like coloured glass instead of metal.

studio.description: The strip lights, and therefore the bright part of every reflection. Slightly warm by default, because a neutral white room makes the metal read as grey.

roughness.description: How polished. At 0 it is a mirror with the room sharp in it; by about 0.4 the strips have softened into a sheen and it reads as brushed. Past about 0.6 there is nothing left to reflect and it goes to grey.

lamps.description: Strip lights round the room. Two is a photographer's key and fill. More than four and the object has highlights everywhere, which flattens it: the dark between the strips is what gives the form its shape.

height.description: Height of the form in scene units, where the camera frames about four.

waist.description: How far the middle pulls in, as a share of girth. At 0 it is a plain capped barrel. The waist is what gives the reflection somewhere to bend sharply, which is the most metal-looking thing on the object.

tilt.description: Degrees the axis leans. A little off vertical is the difference between an object and a diagram of one.

period.description: Seconds for one full turn. Exactly one turn, so the loop closes with no join.
